⭕️ Resistance, perseverance, and four-dimensional care

To protect Iran against colonial and multi-stage weakening schemes (especially until a new equilibrium is achieved in the region), we need the following simultaneously and in synergy:

1️⃣ Military resistance
2️⃣ Diplomatic resistance
3️⃣ Social perseverance, and
4️⃣ Economic care for the most disadvantaged citizens

Any force that pays insufficient attention to any one of these four dimensions of national resistance and perseverance, and fails to accept what is required to strengthen them all at once, will inadvertently diminish our national endurance and capacity to make it through the formidable passes that lie ahead.

@jalaeipour

The second episode of the Neshan podcast, titled "On the Shores of the Red Sea," has been released. In this episode, we hear how Yemen's fate became intertwined with the decision of the King of Iran. Before the rise of Islam, Yemen had become an arena of rivalry between Iran, Rome, and Abyssinia—a rivalry that was not only about power but also centered on the trade routes of the Red Sea. Amid these conflicts, one of Yemen's notables traveled to the court of Khosrow Anushirvan to seek Iran's help in expelling the Abyssinian rulers. In the second episode of the "Neshan" podcast, we learn the story of a small army from Iran that marched on Yemen—an event that led to the formation of the Iranian community in Yemen and left traces that endured into the early years of Islam. You can now listen to this episode on Castbox and Shenoto. entry.title: [jalaeipour] Being Iranian is a blend of wisdom, justice, liberty, and love—four pillars…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @jalaeipour

Being Iranian is a blend of wisdom, justice, liberty, and love—four pillars on which our culture rests. A culture's pillars should not be judged merely by how faithfully people adhere to them today; we must also ask what values a culture possesses that enable it to recognize and correct its own shortcomings. These four pillars are not a claim that Iranians are flawless; they are an ethical and cultural horizon we can lean on to build a better society. Wisdom, justice, liberty, and love are neither imported values nor newly invented ideals; they are rooted in our own history and intellectual and cultural heritage. From the Avesta and the teachings of truth and asha, to the admonition books of ancient Iran and their emphasis on wisdom and justice; from Ferdowsi's Shahnameh and its praise of wisdom, justice, and liberty, to the works of Saadi and other great figures of Persian literature who have honored love and humanism—the continuity of these values is visible. These four pillars are not meant to describe the behavior of all Iranians in all eras. They are criteria rooted in our culture, and we can even draw on them to critique the shortcomings of today's society. If there is foolishness, wisdom remains a virtue; if there is injustice, justice remains a value; if there is baseness and flattery, liberty remains an ideal; and if there is violence and hatred, love remains an ethical necessity.

⭕️ The need for greater caution among military and civilian officials to avoid assassination in the coming weeks

Despite certain warnings, it was wrongly assumed that America would not assassinate General Soleimani during his trip to Iraq. Unfortunately, it did. We lost our strongest strategic commander. Despite warning signs, it was wrongly assumed that Israel/America would not assassinate our top-tier military commanders in Tehran in the middle of negotiations. Sufficient caution was not taken, and unfortunately, on a single day and sometimes in a single above-ground location within firing range, a group of our most capable commanders were assassinated on the first day of the 12-day war, and we lost martyrs of the caliber of Major General Bagheri and Major General Rashid.

Despite numerous warning signs, it was wrongly assumed that Israel/America would not be so foolish and audacious as to assassinate the Commander-in-Chief and a source of emulation whose martyrdom injects unprecedented strength and blood into the homeland resistance. It committed exactly such folly and audacity, and we lost Iran's martyred leader on the first day of the Ramadan war.

Despite the high risk and bare-minimum protective measures, meetings of military and security commanders were held "above ground" all at once and became assassination targets, and on the first day of the Ramadan war we lost a large number of our most elite commanders and officials. It was obvious that national politicians of the caliber of Ali Larijani — who have the capacity to create leverage and open paths without abandoning the requirements of national power — were exposed to Israeli assassination. Even so, sufficient caution was again not taken, and he was placed "above ground" within firing range, and we lost the martyr Larijani.

From today until at least Dey 10 (the start of the new Democratic Congress), it is also clear that the risk of assassination by Israel or America is high, yet unfortunately, again and again and without sufficient caution, high-ranking civilian and military officials gather at funeral ceremonies at Masjid-e Noor, exhibitions, trips, and meetings — and even the meetings of the heads of the branches are held above ground.

Martyrdom in the path of Iran and the collective good of Iranians is an honor, and the courage of officials in high-risk conditions is commendable; but national responsibility and the damage that the assassination of any national figure in the current conditions inflicts on the country — learning from the above miscalculations and from the proven ability of the criminal Israel to carry out terrorist operations — demands that in the coming weeks, far more than today, protective precautions be observed regarding the location of meetings and high-risk, unnecessary programs. Respected officials! Dear commanders! Please, for the sake of Iran, in these weeks exercise far greater caution and care so that you are not assassinated by Israel or America. The conditions are not normal. @jalaeipour
